title: VLAN Configuration Issue
symptom: VLAN configuration prevents expected host communication.
topology_note: Standard access-switch topology; VLAN membership is the suspected fault.
show_command_output: show vlan brief; show interfaces switchport; ping
expected_fault: VLAN configuration is incorrect

title: VLAN Assignment Issue
symptom: Host cannot communicate because its switchport is assigned to the wrong VLAN.
topology_note: PC connected to an access port on a 2960 switch.
show_command_output: show vlan brief; show interfaces switchport; ping
expected_fault: Switchport is assigned to the wrong access VLAN

title: Trunk Configuration Issue
symptom: VLAN traffic fails across a required trunk link.
topology_note: VLAN traffic must cross the trunk between network devices.
show_command_output: show interfaces trunk; show interfaces switchport; ping
expected_fault: Trunk configuration is incorrect

title: Missing VLAN
symptom: Required VLAN is absent from the switch.
topology_note: Required VLAN must exist before access ports can use it.
expected_fault: Required VLAN is missing

title: Wrong Switchport Mode
symptom: Expected VLAN connectivity fails because a switchport uses the wrong mode.
topology_note: Host-facing port requires access mode.
expected_fault: Switchport mode is incorrect

title: Wrong Default Gateway
symptom: PC0 cannot reach the remote network because its gateway is 192.168.10.254 instead of 192.168.10.1.
topology_note: PC0–Switch0–Router0–Router1–Switch1–PC1; PC0 is on 192.168.10.0/24.
show_command_output: ipconfig; show ip interface brief; show ip route; ping
expected_fault: PC0 has an incorrect default gateway

title: Missing Default Gateway
symptom: PC0 cannot reach the remote network because no default gateway is configured.
topology_note: Two-router routed topology; PC0 gateway intentionally blank.
expected_fault: PC0 default gateway is missing

title: Wrong Router LAN IP
symptom: PC0 expects gateway 192.168.20.1, but Router0 G0/0 is 192.168.20.254.
topology_note: PC0 is connected to Router0 LAN through Switch0.
show_command_output: show ip interface brief; ipconfig; ping
expected_fault: Router LAN interface has an incorrect IP address

title: DHCP Pool Wrong Network
symptom: DHCP clients cannot obtain an address because the pool uses the wrong network.
topology_note: Router0 provides DHCP for 192.168.40.0/24 clients.
expected_fault: DHCP pool network is incorrect

title: DHCP Excluded Address Mistake
symptom: DHCP clients cannot obtain an address because the entire client subnet is excluded.
topology_note: Router0 DHCP pool serves 192.168.40.0/24.
expected_fault: DHCP excluded-address range covers the client subnet

title: DHCP Relay Missing
symptom: Remote DHCP client cannot obtain an address because the relay/helper is missing.
topology_note: PC0 LAN is 192.168.20.0/24; DHCP server is Router2 across a routed link.
expected_fault: ip helper-address is missing on Router0 G0/0

title: Wrong DHCP Default Gateway
symptom: DHCP assigns PC0 an incorrect default gateway.
topology_note: Router2 supplies DHCP options to the remote 192.168.20.0/24 client network.
show_command_output: show ip dhcp pool; ipconfig; ping
expected_fault: DHCP pool default-router option is incorrect

title: Wrong DNS Server
symptom: PC0 cannot resolve test.local because it uses the wrong DNS server.
topology_note: Server0 at 192.168.40.20 hosts the test.local DNS record.
expected_fault: PC0 DNS server is incorrectly configured

title: DNS Service Disabled
symptom: Name resolution fails because the DNS service on Server0 is disabled.
topology_note: Server0 hosts test.local; DNS service is intentionally switched off.
expected_fault: DNS service is disabled

title: Missing DNS Record
symptom: Name resolution fails because the required DNS record is missing.
topology_note: Server0 DNS service is on but test.local record is removed.
expected_fault: Required DNS record is missing

title: Missing Static Route
symptom: PC0 cannot reach 192.168.40.0/24 because Router0 lacks a route.
topology_note: Two-router static-routing topology.
expected_fault: Static route to 192.168.40.0/24 is missing

title: Wrong Static Route Next Hop
symptom: PC0 cannot reach the remote network because the static route uses an incorrect next hop.
topology_note: Router0 route to 192.168.40.0/24 points to a directly connected but nonexistent host.
expected_fault: Static route next hop is incorrect

title: OSPF Network Statement Missing
symptom: Router2 does not advertise its LAN into OSPF.
topology_note: Router2 advertises the transit network but not 192.168.40.0/24 after the fault.
show_command_output: show ip ospf; show ip route; ping
expected_fault: OSPF network statement for 192.168.40.0/24 is missing

title: Incorrect Subnet Mask on Routed Interface
symptom: OSPF adjacency fails because Router2 G0/0 uses /24 instead of /30.
topology_note: Router0–Router2 transit network is 10.0.0.0/30.
show_command_output: show ip interface brief; show ip ospf neighbor
expected_fault: Router2 G0/0 has an incorrect subnet mask

title: ACL Blocks Required Traffic
symptom: PC0-to-PC2 traffic is blocked by an explicit ACL deny.
topology_note: ACL 100 is applied outbound on Router0 G0/1.
show_command_output: show access-lists; show ip interface gigabitEthernet0/1; ping
expected_fault: Extended ACL denies traffic from 192.168.20.0/24 to 192.168.40.0/24

title: ACL Applied to Wrong Interface/Direction
symptom: ACL is applied in the wrong direction, so intended traffic is not filtered.
topology_note: ACL 101 is applied inbound on Router0 G0/1; source traffic enters via G0/0.
show_command_output: show ip interface gigabitEthernet0/1; show access-lists; ping
expected_fault: ACL is applied in the wrong interface/direction

title: Missing Permit Statement
symptom: Traffic is blocked because the ACL contains a deny rule without a permit statement.
topology_note: ACL 102 has only a deny entry and therefore ends with implicit deny.
expected_fault: Required permit statement is missing; implicit deny blocks traffic

title: NAT Inside/Outside Interfaces Reversed
symptom: NAT fails because Router0 inside and outside interface roles are reversed.
topology_note: PC0 is the inside network and Router0 G0/1 is the outside/transit interface.
show_command_output: show ip nat statistics; show ip interface; ping
expected_fault: NAT inside/outside roles are reversed

title: NAT ACL Does Not Match Inside Subnet
symptom: NAT fails because the ACL permits the wrong inside subnet.
topology_note: Actual inside subnet is 192.168.50.0/24; ACL incorrectly permits 192.168.60.0/24.
show_command_output: show access-lists; show ip nat statistics; ping
expected_fault: NAT ACL does not match the actual inside subnet

title: NAT Overload Missing
symptom: NAT fails because the PAT/overload rule has been removed.
topology_note: Correct NAT inside/outside interfaces and ACL remain configured.
show_command_output: show ip nat statistics; show ip nat translations; ping
expected_fault: NAT overload rule is missing

title: Wrong Wireless SSID
symptom: Laptop cannot connect because the AP SSID does not match the client SSID.
topology_note: AP broadcasts WRONG_SSID while the laptop is configured for NETSAGE.
expected_fault: AP SSID does not match the client SSID

title: Wrong WPA2 Password
symptom: Laptop cannot connect because AP and client WPA2 credentials differ.
topology_note: AP uses WrongPass123 while laptop retains NetSage123.
expected_fault: WPA2-PSK credentials do not match

title: AP Connected to Wrong VLAN
symptom: Wireless connectivity fails because AP switchport is in VLAN 20 while Router2 remains in VLAN 10.
topology_note: AP on Switch2 Fa0/1; Router2 on Fa0/24; intended wireless VLAN is 10.
expected_fault: AP switchport is assigned to the wrong VLAN

title: Wireless Interface Disabled
symptom: Wireless client connectivity fails because the AP wireless interface is disabled.
topology_note: AP Port 1 wireless status is OFF.
expected_fault: Wireless interface is disabled

title: DHCP Unavailable for Wireless Clients
symptom: Wireless laptop cannot obtain an address because the WIRELESS DHCP pool is unavailable.
topology_note: Laptop uses DHCP on 192.168.40.0/24; Router2 normally provides the WIRELESS pool.
expected_fault: Wireless DHCP pool/service is unavailable
